carcassonne: a row of small dark stone cells along a corridor in a medieval prison building, heavy wooden doors with iron bands, a chain fixed to one wall, a bread loaf and water jug on the floor
loches: a vaulted stone room in a castle keep holding a small cage made of heavy wooden beams plated with iron straps, its door padlocked, a slit window high in the wall
daliborka: the inside of a round stone artillery tower: an upper cell with a small window and a tiled stove, and below it, through an opening in the floor, a dark round lower dungeon
chillon: a long dim Gothic vaulted undercroft cut partly from the rock, below the level of the lake outside, a row of stout plain stone columns with nothing attached to them, only small high slit openings letting in faint light, a bare rock floor
castel-sant-angelo: the massive round central keep of a Roman mausoleum turned fortress, seen in cutaway with a small prison room high up, and one single long flat band of linen strips sewn end to end, smooth with no knots, hanging from one point on the roof parapet down the outer wall
st-andrews: a bottle-shaped pit cut down into solid rock beneath a tower vault, about seven metres deep, its only opening a narrow neck at the top closed by a trapdoor in the vault floor
nuremberg: a low vaulted cellar beneath a town hall with a row of tiny cells about two metres square, lined entirely with wooden planks, each with a plank bed and bench, an iron heating basin in the corridor
little-ease: a cross-section through the massive stone foundations of a great Norman tower showing one very small cramped niche of a cell, barely four feet high and four feet deep, so low a person could not stand and so short they could not lie down, with a small three-legged stool inside for scale and a heavy studded door filling its front; the surrounding masonry is enormous and solid, making the cell look tiny
cachtice: a plain room in a hilltop castle with thick plastered walls, an ordinary wooden door, a small barred window, a simple bed, table and chair, the ruined castle walls and wooded hills visible beyond; nothing bricked up
lancaster: an underground stone dungeon beneath a castle tower, a low vaulted room with a heavy door at the top of worn steps, straw on the floor and a narrow air shaft
pignerol: a stone room in an Alpine citadel with a barred window looking onto snowy mountains, a writing table with books and a chair, a heavy locked door
iron-mask: a stone cell in the Bastille with a narrow window, a bed and a chair, and on the table a plain black velvet mask lying folded
dunnottar: a single long vaulted stone cellar below a building on a cliff-top castle, one small window opening onto the sea far below, a bare earthen floor
peter-paul: a plain early-eighteenth-century guardhouse room inside a brick and stone island fortress, a wooden bench, a large tiled masonry stove in the corner, a small window looking onto a broad river and a slender spire
marshalsea: a crowded brick-walled debtors' ward about sixteen by fourteen feet, hammocks slung in rows above straw pallets on the floor, a single small window
newgate: a crowded eighteenth-century courtroom next to a gaol, judges in wigs on a raised bench, a packed public gallery, and through an open door the dark passage to the prison, with a large wooden ventilator on the roof above
magdeburg: a small vaulted casemate cell inside thick fortress walls, shut by several heavy doors, a thick iron staple set in the wall with heavy chains hanging from it and a brick seat beneath, a water jug, no prisoner shown
black-hole-calcutta: a small square guardroom cell about eighteen feet across with solid walls on three sides and two small windows strongly barred with iron on the fourth, a heavy door, empty, a hot still night outside
piombi-casanova: attic cells beneath a steep roof covered in lead sheets, the cells made of thick wooden partitions studded with nails and plated with iron, a small hole broken through the ceiling planks, the rooftops of Venice beyond
chateau-d-if: a square three-storey stone fort with round towers on a bare limestone island in the sea, cut away to show a dark damp cell at the base of a tower and a better furnished room with a bed and table on the floor above
mont-saint-michel-cage: a dark damp vaulted stone cell in an abbey on a rock, holding a cage built of thick wooden beams with a heavy door, a flower scratched into one post
bastille: the inside of one eight-sided tower room of a great fortress prison in the 1780s, with a stone fireplace, a bed, a table and chair and a single barred window, the massive walls three metres thick
iron-maiden-nuremberg: a museum gallery in the 1800s with a tall hinged iron cabinet shaped roughly like a woman, its doors open showing spikes inside, displayed on a plinth beside glass cases of old objects
oubliette: a narrow round shaft dropping from a trapdoor in a vaulted castle floor into a dark pit below, drawn as a cross-section, the pit plainly empty except for a few storage barrels, suggesting it may be a store room
bridge-of-sighs: a small enclosed bridge of pale limestone arching high over a narrow canal between a grand Gothic palace and a plain heavy prison block, with two small windows filled with stone grilles, drawn in cutaway to show the cramped double corridor inside
clitherow: a small stone tollhouse room on a medieval bridge over a river, with a bare flagstone floor, a heavy beam ceiling and one small window onto the water, and a plain wooden house door leaning against the wall; the room is empty
fawkes: a stone chamber inside a great medieval fortress, with a heavy timber door, small leaded windows looking onto a river, and a plain table holding a quill, an inkpot and a folded letter sealed with wax; the room is empty
shlisselburg: a low island fortress of grey stone walls and squat round towers on broad water under a pale northern sky, cut away to show inside one small whitewashed cell with a single high barred window and a narrow cot
